goal: A theory of why trained networks generalize that predicts, explains, scales and is certified; and a verified compiler that makes its predictions computable.

effective_when.name: Predicts
effective_when.test: On tasks outside the class it was fitted on, including real data, the theory predicts held-out behaviour better than the kernel baseline, in a pre-registered test.

effective_when.name: Explains
effective_when.test: The pull toward the minimum circuit is derived from the training dynamics (a theorem or a quantitative law verified prospectively), not only observed.

effective_when.name: Scales
effective_when.test: The same result holds at n ≥ 8 inputs and beyond width 8, with compiler-computed completions.

effective_when.name: Certified
effective_when.test: Every claim the theory rests on is machine-checked or pre-registered and replicated; the ledger shows no claim stated stronger than its support.

gaps.title: Other target classes
gaps.have: The Occam pull holds on three further clean classes at n = 6: cost-4 targets 0.72, symmetric functions 0.90, DNF 0.67 (Spike 45). The class where it weakens is characterized: label noise (0.58).
gaps.missing: Nothing for clean targets. The noise boundary is tracked as gap A8.
gaps.closes_when: Pre-registered: Occam sides with the net ≥ 0.65 on at least 3 further target classes, or the class where it fails is characterized.

gaps.title: Real data: the theory currently fails there
gaps.have: Pre-registered test on four real datasets (Spike 45): the Occam pull holds only on Wine (0.74); it is broken on Breast Cancer (0.29) and Diabetes (0.45). The kernel predicts the net better than Occam on 3 of 4, and beats the trained net on 3 of 4.
gaps.missing: A version of the theory that predicts trained nets on noisy real tasks better than the kernel does.
gaps.closes_when: Pre-registered on the same four datasets plus two new ones: a stated predictor agrees with trained nets more than the kernel does in at least 4 of 6.
gaps.next: After A8: test the noise-tolerant minimum circuit on these datasets

gaps.title: Label noise: where the Occam pull breaks
gaps.have: One noisy synthetic cell (5 of 48 labels flipped): pull 0.58, against 0.67–0.90 on clean classes. Real tasks, which are noisy, fail.
gaps.missing: A dose–response in the noise level, and a test of conjecture C20: nets follow the cheapest circuit that is allowed to misfit some labels, not the exact-fit one.
gaps.closes_when: Pre-registered: (a) the pull falls monotonically with the number of flipped labels; (b) a noise-tolerant minimum circuit sides with the net ≥ 0.65 at the noise level where the exact-fit one is ≤ 0.60.

gaps.title: Mechanism: why feature learning finds small circuits
gaps.have: Correlation (73–81%), one causal arm (lazy regime moves nets back to the kernel), and timing (kernel first, Occam from step ~30).
gaps.missing: A derivation. The unit-level selection law (volume × information tilt) is not shown to produce the Occam pull (C18 not supported).
gaps.closes_when: A stated law that predicts the Occam-sides fraction or S(t) from measurable quantities, confirmed in a prospective test.
gaps.next: After A8: the mechanism must also explain why noise removes the pull

gaps.title: One predictor for the net's held-out outputs
gaps.have: Three separate predictors at n = 6: kernel 0.80 agreement, Occam 0.90; at n = 5 nets beat Occam on accuracy.
gaps.missing: A single rule combining kernel and circuit cost that predicts each held-out output, and explains where nets beat Occam.
gaps.closes_when: Pre-registered: per-input agreement with trained nets ≥ 0.93 at n = 6 on fresh tasks.

gaps.title: Two-phase timing replicated
gaps.have: One cell (n = 6, tanh, width 8); the first-step criterion fell short (0.77 vs 0.80).

gaps.title: Scale: n ≥ 8
gaps.have: Everything is at n ≤ 6. Width was varied only toward the lazy regime.
gaps.missing: Occam completions at n = 8–10, which need care-set compilation at scale (gap B2).
gaps.closes_when: The Spike 36 protocol at n ≥ 8 with certified or bounded Occam completions.

gaps.title: Depth on targets that need it
gaps.have: Depth adds no Occam pull when two layers can represent the target (H-K refuted).
gaps.missing: Targets that need three layers (e.g. parity5).
gaps.closes_when: The Spike 44 protocol on depth-requiring targets.

gaps.title: Lean check of nets beyond fan-in 4
gaps.have: A Lean checker for threshold nets; xor3 passes in 219 s, xor4 times out.
gaps.missing: A linear pseudo-Boolean encoding in Lean (the current one is exponential in fan-in).
gaps.closes_when: xor4 verified by pure kernel `decide` in under 60 s.

gaps.title: Care-set compilation at scale
gaps.have: CP-SAT compiles partial functions to n = 6 with certificates; the Ur-Compiler handles total, factored functions to n = 16.
gaps.missing: Minimum (or bounded) circuits for partial functions at n = 8–10.
gaps.closes_when: ≥ 90% of n = 8 care-set tasks compiled with a lower-bound certificate within 60 s each.

gaps.title: Minimality certificates
gaps.have: Gate counts against a flat-BDD baseline; parity4 ≥ 5 neurons is uncertified.
gaps.missing: Lower bounds for Ur-Compiler outputs; the parity4 certificate.
gaps.closes_when: parity4 ≥ 5 certified; Ur-Compiler outputs carry a bound.

gaps.title: Theorem 15 in Lean
gaps.missing: Mechanization. It is the weakest link behind 20 ledger notes.
gaps.closes_when: Lean proof with standard axioms; the ledger notes resting on P069 clear.

gaps.title: No-transfer lemma in Lean
gaps.missing: Mechanization (6 ledger notes rest on it).

gaps.title: Statistical lift (C1) with real probability
gaps.have: Arithmetic scaffolding in Lean; 0/48 false rejections in an exploratory run.
gaps.closes_when: A proved finite-sample bound, or a pre-registered test of the conjectured rate.

gaps.title: C4 converse and C3 rank bound
gaps.have: One inclusion of C4; a lower bound for C3.
gaps.missing: The converse inclusion for separable queries; the rank bound on the adaptivity gap.

gaps.title: Replicate Gemini's unregistered results
gaps.have: Six spikes run without pre-registration; their claims are held as exploratory. The real-data question was re-run under pre-registration in Spike 45.
gaps.missing: Pre-registered replications of the ones the theory would use (width compression 86–89%; real-data circuits).
gaps.closes_when: Each used result is replicated under rule 1 or dropped.

gaps.title: One intermittently failing test
gaps.have: Diagnosed as Monte-Carlo variance (mean 0.95, min 0.875 against a 0.9 bar).
gaps.missing: A deterministic version of the test.
gaps.closes_when: The suite passes on every run.
